correctness.rationale: Jongeneel's Proposition 3.5 was inspected in full at the example and Hessian contradiction. The standard scalar \(a(x)=\exp(-1/\|x\|^2)\) off the origin is smooth and flat, so both constructed vector fields have zero complete Taylor jet. The radial field has an exact quadratic Morse Lyapunov function. For the time-changed no-Morse field, global asymptotic stability follows from the positive orbit-preserving reparameterization, and any putative Morse Lyapunov function would also certify the original source field after division of its strict orbital derivative by \(a(x)>0\). No finite experiment or numerical certificate is used.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly leaves complete characterization open and notes that higher-order effects are unclear. The construction rules out an entire class of prospective criteria at once: no criterion depending only on a finite jet or even the full formal Taylor series can decide Morse–Lyapunov existence for smooth GAS planar fields. This identifies a structural boundary of local formal information rather than a routine example or parameter change.
